title: POC scoping — model shortlist & workload sizing (SummitWave Analytics)
summary: Quick scoping call to align success criteria, expected workload, and pick an open-model shortlist for a 6-week POC focused on multilingual customer support routing and domain-specific summarization. Discussed tradeoffs (latency vs cost, quantization impact); agreed on benchmarks (latency p95, token cost, quality on 3 prompt sets) and timeline with a 2-week bench sprint then 4-week eval. Next: Redwood to share benchmark plan and price estimate; SummitWave to share 5k anonymized transcripts and priority prompt sets.
next_steps: Redwood: send artifact — benchmark plan + model shortlist + cost estimate by 2028-03-06
SummitWave: upload 5k anonymized transcripts and label schema to shared S3 by 2028-03-09
Schedule bench kickoff (30m) for 2028-03-10 with AE+SE+SummitWave ML team
action_items: Maya Patel - Share benchmark spreadsheet and proposed evaluation prompts - 2028-03-06
Marcus Reed - Provide anonymized transcripts (5k) and priority labels - 2028-03-09
Eric Zhao - Prepare initial model binary/runner for internal bench (quantized variant) - 2028-03-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Eric (Redwood SE), Tom (Redwood SA); Lena (CTO), Marcus (Lead ML Eng), Sofia (PM), Jamal (Infra)

Auto Summary: quick alignment on success metrics and model shortlist; bench sprint + eval timeline agreed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. quick roundtable — could you each say hi and your role?
[00:12] Lena: Lena Ortiz, CTO, summitwave. we're trying to automate first‑line support routing and also generate tl;dr summaries of chats, and multilingual is kinda a hard requirement.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus Reed, Lead ML, I'll be hands on for the POC and we'll own the data prep and labeling.
[00:25] Sofia: Sofia Park, PM, i'm owner of the success criteria and timeline.
[00:28] Jamal: Jamal Singh, infra, i'll quiz on VPC, network egress, and any KMS.
[00:33] Maya: awesome. quick context from us — Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated pools, and private deployment. for a POC we typically suggest starting hosted to iterate fast, but if you need VPC early we can do private. noting that you said multilingual — that's a key factor for model choice.
[01:00] Eric: hi all. i'm Eric. for the bench i'm thinking we run three workloads: routing (classification/intent), summarization (multi‑turn), and a rerank/recall test. measure p95 latency per request, cost per 1k tokens, and quality via our rubric (accuracy/F1 for routing, ROUGE or human score for summaries).
[01:28] Marcus: sounds right. quick question on throughput — our production target is about 120 qps at peak but initial POC load is around 5 qps, we want to ensure chosen model can scale and we can estimate cost.
[01:42] Tom: good note. we'll size bench instances to simulate both 5 qps and a scaled 100–150 qps scenario. rough rule: smaller model quantized 4bit will shave cost but may degrade some language nuance, especially in FR and ES.
[02:10] Lena: tradeoffs — accuracy vs cost is core. our success metric: routing accuracy within 3% of current human baseline and summary helpfulness > 85% (via quick human eval) within the POC. if we hit those, we consider pilot.
[02:28] Maya: nice crisp success criteria. timeline idea? we suggested 2 weeks bench sprint then 4 weeks eval to decide. is that realistic?
[02:36] Sofia: yes 6 weeks total seems fine — product wants a decision by mid‑April.
[02:41] Jamal: about security — we need SOC2 type II evidence, SSO via SAML, and audit logs stored for 1 year. can Redwood meet that?
[02:51] Maya: Redwood has SOC2 and SSO integrations; we can share the compliance pack. audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with retention add‑ons. i'll attach the doc.
[03:05] Marcus: okay good. now model shortlist — what are you proposing for open models? and can you show our expected quality tradeoffs across EN/ES/FR?
[03:14] Eric: proposed shortlist: 1) Llama‑X‑Large (baseline), 2) Mistral‑Open‑7B variant, 3) Mosaic‑M2‑Base (quantized), 4) multilingual‑opt (a smaller dedicated multilingual model). i'll share relative bench expectations: Llama‑X best raw English quality, Mistral competitive cost/quality, Mosaic very cheap when quantized but drops on paraphrase and nuance, multilingual‑opt best for FR/ES but larger latency.
[03:50] Lena: any examples of where quantization killed quality? we care about legal/regulatory language — small shifts in wording matter.
[03:59] Eric: yes, on summarization we've seen 4bit quantization introduce hallucination risk in long context; KC cache [sic] and kv cache behavior also affects long‑chat summarization — you'll see differences in p95 for long traces. for legal like you said, we might keep the non‑quantized path for those prompts or run hybrid: quantized for routing, full precision for summary.
[04:30] Marcus: hybrid makes sense. also, can we test instruction‑tuning variants? some of our prompts are heavy system instructions.
[04:37] Tom: yes instruction‑tuned variants generally help, we'll include a tuned checkpoint where available.
[04:44] Sofia: about benchmarks — what metrics exactly will you run? latency numbers at different token lengths?
[04:49] Eric: we'll report p50/p95 latency for short (<=64 tokens), medium (65–512), and long (512–2048) sequences, cost per 1k input+output tokens, throughput at batch sizes 1, 8, 16, and a quality sweep with your 3 prompt sets: routing, customer support summary, and escalation detection. also memory/kv cache miss rate for long chats.
[05:20] Jamal: networking — if we choose Private, is there an on‑prem option? we need an air‑gapped possibility for certain projects.
[05:26] Tom: yes we offer on‑prem packages; the private control plane can run in your VPC and we support bring‑your‑own KMS/HSM. there are sizing and firewall rules we'll send.
[05:40] Lena: good. pricing — can you give a ballpark for cost delta between Large unquantized and 4bit quantized?
[05:47] Maya: ballpark: quantized 4bit can be 3–4x cheaper per token; Dedicated committed capacity reduces unit cost further. exact depends on batching, cache hit rates, and sequence length. we'll surface an estimate in the spreadsheet.
[06:05] Marcus: for the bench data — we'll provide 5k transcripts across EN/ES/FR with labels, and a subset of 200 longer chats for summarization.
[06:14] Eric: perfect. we'll run bench tests on your data to get realistic numbers. can you confirm sample proportions per language?
[06:20] Marcus: roughly 70% EN, 20% ES, 10% FR.
[06:24] Eric: got it. we'll ensure multilingual‑opt is included because sometimes models trained for EN degrade nonlinearly on ES/FR.
[06:33] Sofia: what about SLA expectations for pilot versus prod?
[06:36] Maya: pilot we'll be best‑effort with monitoring; if you go Dedicated/pilot conversion we can commit to a latency SLA and uptime. we'll document.
[06:45] Lena: any constraints on data retention during the POC? GDPR concerns for EU customers — we may need EU region processing.
[06:52] Tom: we can run inference in EU regions for data residency; Private deployment is the most straightforward path for strict residency and retention controls.
[07:00] Jamal: ok. who will run the bench? Redwood or us?
[07:03] Eric: Redwood will run baseline bench on the provided dataset and provide results + runner configs. if you want to run in your VPC, we can provide a bench runner artifact and instructions.
[07:12] Marcus: i'd like us to run one replicate in our VPC to validate network and latency.
[07:15] Tom: noted — we'll provide a dockerized runner and perf harness.
[07:20] Maya: recap — items and timeline: Redwood sends benchmark plan, model shortlist, and pricing by 2028‑03‑06. bench kickoff 2028‑03‑10. SummitWave uploads data by 2028‑03‑09. initial bench results by 2028‑03‑24, then 4‑week evaluation finishing mid‑April.
[07:38] Sofia: agreed. also please share the SOC2 pack and SSO instructions.
[07:44] Maya: will do. also sharing a short note — for POC we'll instrument cost telemetry (token breakdown) in Redwood Console so you can see unit costs per route.
[07:55] Marcus: perfect. one last technical — will we be able to pin exact model checkpoints for A/B? we may want to test two checkpoints in parallel.
[08:02] Eric: yes, we support canary/AB rollouts and pin model versions per route. we'll include rollout configs in the bench artifact.
[08:10] Lena: thanks everyone, this was helpful. excited to see the bench results.
[08:15] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up with the pack and the spreadsheet.

--- End Transcript ---
